reviews.text: I found Nope to be a compelling analysis of our relationship with entertainment and addiction to spectacle.
reviews.author: Isabella Liistro

reviews.text: This may be Peele’s version of a summer blockbuster, but it goes well beyond popcorn entertainment.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: Nope is jam-packed with allegories, messages, and tension-filled moments, but does it arrange all of those coherently without feeling overinflated? Nope.
reviews.author: Justin Kim

reviews.text: I can’t confidently say that everything works, but most of Peele’s latest feels as experimental and creative as it is simple and fun.
reviews.author: Brittany Patrice Witherspoon

reviews.text: With unflinching dexterity, Peele and cinematographer Hoyte van Hoytema juxtapose the terror of encountering a being from beyond with one of the most claustrophobic scenes ever caught on film.
reviews.author: Joe George

reviews.text: Nope‘s combination of stellar acting, incredible cinematography and awesome sound design makes this a cinematic experience that’s out of this world.
reviews.author: Ygraine Hackett-Cantabrana

reviews.text: Jordan Peele crafted an impressively well-crafted sci-fi flick that while it displays clear homage to classics, feels unlike anything we’ve seen before it.
reviews.author: Shakyl Lambert

reviews.text: Nope is simply put one of the year's best films
reviews.author: Paul Klein

reviews.text: Jordan Peele’s mind is astonishing. He takes such large concepts and layers them upon each other, building out a metaphorical journey that only deepens with each viewing.
reviews.author: Zach Youngs

reviews.text: “Nope” is really a story about the underdogs in showbiz trying to survive instead of getting out, but Peele pulls punches when it comes to showing how demented they are in that pursuit.
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: The supporting players work together in ways that show Peele’s prowess, not only as a visual filmmaker, but as one who casts well and trusts his actors. Nope is a wild ride, and one I can’t wait to take again.
reviews.author: Dave Giannini

reviews.text: Jordan Peele’s third film captures the terrible beauty of our endless fascination with events no matter how horrific.
reviews.author: Mini Anthikad-Chhibber

reviews.text: Nope, Peele’s third directorial outing, may debut in the horror genre, but there’s more to the brilliant film than audiences’ expectations.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Peterson

reviews.text: More stylish than substantial.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: I love all of Jordan's movies so far, but this one might be my favorite just because there's so much to unpack. Every time I think about it I find more things that I need to talk about and it's the gift that keeps giving.
reviews.author: Sharai Bohannon

reviews.text: It's a very layered movie, lot of themes on Hollywood and how it uses people and kinda chews them up and spits them out - figuratively.  He [Jordan Peele] is probably one of our best directors today.
reviews.author: Michael Cook

reviews.text: The failure of Nope is partly because of Peele's lack of restraint in terms of mangling together mismatched ideas.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: Although the vision is stronger than the pen this time around, the Spielberg-esque scope is all-embracing, and his craftiness in the individual horror/sci-fi set pieces is utterly remarkable.
reviews.author: Hector A. Gonzalez

reviews.text: As with his previous films, Peele wears his inspirations on his sleeve. This time around he mines heavily from two Spielberg classics, Close Encounters of the Third Kind and Jaws.
reviews.author: Paul Kanieski

reviews.text: Jordan Peele takes full advantage of Hoyte van Hoytema's phenomenal cinematography and Michael Abels' memorable score to create a spectacle worthy of the big screen, but it's the sound production that really elevates the movie to that level.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: An almost perfect spectacle that dives into our obsessions with spectacles in our real life. A unique blockbuster that will make you afraid of looking up.
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: Jordan Peele has made a science fiction thriller that is one of the most visually striking films in recent memory.
reviews.author: Matthew Creith

reviews.text: Known for his powerful social commentary in US and Get Out, Jordan Peele reinvents the summer blockbuster through a neo-sci-fi western that looks at society’s obsession with spectacle.
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: Damn the white-washed history, and the capitalist traps of Hollywood’s fortune and fame. The beast has no more power here.
reviews.author: Brooke Obie

reviews.text: It's a good movie, but perhaps it's time to take some of our bloated expectations off Peele as a filmmaker.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: The film ultimately spends what feels like an eternity in a climactic and rather confusing confrontation that feels elaborate but fails to ratchet up the tension.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: A sci-fi horror flick that raises some interesting questions about why aliens might come to Earth and what for.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: Director-writer Peele clearly knows the business of suspending disbelief. I say “yup” to ‘Nope.’
reviews.author: Steve Crum

reviews.text: Beneath the interesting and strange tale of aliens and UAPs is Peele shining a bright light from the sky onto Hollywood and American pop culture’s exploitation of Black people and animals.
reviews.author: C.H. Newell

reviews.text: There's so much considered detail and nuance that is weaved into these fantastical themes which is bolstered by a lot of the characters taking control of their own narrative.
reviews.author: KT Mahe

reviews.text: I've never felt that before. It was a completely new feeling especially in the sci-fi horror genre where you just don't get a lot of Black happiness and Black people and Black camaraderie.
reviews.author: Oti

reviews.text: This final confrontation is truly a spectacle...
reviews.author: Robert Koehler

reviews.text: Feels like a modern take on a classic sci-fi story that would have made a really fantastic episode of The Twilight Zone.
reviews.author: Patrick Hicks

reviews.text: Jordan Peele's Nope innovatively uses the IMAX format in ways many wouldn't have believed possible to create an inescapably immersive experience.
reviews.author: William Jones

reviews.text: To say I was horrified isn’t quite the right word, but Nope gave me that queasy, funny feeling only Peele knows how to create.
reviews.author: Steph Cozza

reviews.text: There are few experiences more thrilling in cinema these days than watching a Jordan Peele film, and Nope is without question his biggest effort so far in terms of scale and spectacle.
reviews.author: Mitchell Beaupre

reviews.text: Nope continues Peele’s winning streak of smart, surprising, and hugely effective thrillers.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: NOPE has ground breaking cinematography and sound design. If seen in theaters or under surround sound, you truly feel like something is out there. Palmer and Kaluuya have great performances, but it was Steve Yeun's character that was most engaging here
reviews.author: Samuel Leggett Jr.

reviews.text: Nope establishes Jordan Peele as an auteur, with a unique perspective in telling stories cinematically! Don’t worry folks, if you think you saw the movie in the final trailers, you don’t know what you’re in for.
reviews.author: Kevin Sampson

reviews.text: Brandon Perea quickly became one of our favorite new performances of the year thanks to his fantastic comedic timing in Nope...five stars, Angel, five stars.
reviews.author: Fletcher Peters

reviews.text: It's a spectacle about spectacle, and about the gambles we'll take to create it and monetize it. That quest lies at the heart of American culture. Nope suggests it's a quest that might eat us all alive.
reviews.author: Ella Feldman

reviews.text: Beautiful and terrifying.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: This is a film full of symbolic exhortations, which is as much a part of the goals of science-fiction as it is essential to Peele’s cinematic oeuvre.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: If you’re expecting another Get Out or Us, you’ll be sorely disappointed. But if given the chance to enjoy it for what it is, then you’ll be saying Nope is dope! That’s a huge yep from me.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: Closer to the slick visuals of “Get Out” but with a more probing narrative, akin to “Us,” “Nope” is as much an experience as all of Peele’s efforts, with a similarly intriguing premise.
reviews.author: Candice Frederick

reviews.text: “Nope” is another equally thrilling and smart ride from the rising director, subtly tackling intersecting ideas about “seeing” and “being seen” along the way.
reviews.author: Dan Schindel

reviews.text: ... layering text and subtext so that audiences can choose to engage with either, deriving pleasure from the tale as either a cinematic spectacle or a profound exploration of humanity’s inability ...
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: Jordan Peel's latest is ambitious and well-made but exhausting and confusing. It's a film full of ideas but it's also stuck in neutral.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: The first hour of Nope is pretty negligible fare with the exception of a flashback to a killer chimpanzee and the wonderful-to-see-again Donna Mills almost getting kicked in the kisser by an upset steed.
reviews.author: Brandon Judell

reviews.text: Nope is full of fun, freaky, thoughtful re-imaginings of the classic UFO movie loaded with creepy monsters, silly characters, and high-stakes action sequences.
reviews.author: Jonathan DeHaan

reviews.text: The odd pacing and ofttimes disjointed storytelling will be off-putting to some, but they're in the service of a variety of knotty themes.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: It's a comment on Hollywood and how people are wasted, swallowed up, disfigured in the name of entertainment. But it’s also foreboding and spooky as hell.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: …a good Saturday night entertainment, but perhaps more was expected from a writer director whose name has become an established brand…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Peele puts the logic-defying risks people take to "capture the moment" and feed society’s obsession the mysterious front and center. It’s dark, twisted and tilts at windmills full throttle.
reviews.author: Ro Moore

reviews.text: Peele has emerged as one of the great living filmmakers by marrying the genre conventions of science fiction and horror with deep, layered social commentary.
reviews.author: Kathryn Reklis

reviews.text: [Nope] takes this word as its title and offers several other interesting usages. All of them suggest that what we’re thinking or saying is absurdly wrong: a proposition that doesn’t need to be made, or that can’t be responded to in any other way.
reviews.author: Michael Wood

reviews.text: Instead of trying to elucidate the plot, it is better to let ourselves be distracted by the images with their allegories and symbolism alluding to Hollywood, and racial and social differences. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gisela Savdie

reviews.text: Working with the fine cinematographer Hoyte van Hoytema, Peele turns the Haywood ranch into a wide-format proscenium of supernatural mayhem.
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: I thought that this was like a well told story, it kept me hooked and engaged all the way to the end.
reviews.author: Jaby Koay

reviews.text: I got the same rush/thrill watching NOPE that I did watching "War of the Worlds"... I found NOPE to be pretty chilling.
reviews.author: Ileana Meléndez

reviews.text: Peele’s direction remains thought provoking whilst utilising jump scares, close framing and the audience’s fear of the unknown to amplify that sensation of unease.
reviews.author: Latoya Austin

reviews.text: Far from perfect, but with more interesting visuals and themes.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Arturo Mora

reviews.text: My best guess is that Nope is an allegory about what happens when we try to profit from forces we barely understand.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: Acclaimed horror filmmaker Jordan Peele's latest film Nope is an attempt at addressing our obsession with spectacle and this insatiable desire to look, rather than look away.
reviews.author: Alex Billington

reviews.text: The first act of Nope is strange, scary, and even a little weird [but] the intrigue doesn't last.
reviews.author: Kristen Maldonado

reviews.text: Despite [Jordan] Peele’s masterful direction in the IMAX-worthy technical areas, he sadly failed what equally matters as well — engaging character arcs and storytelling.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: Here’s the thing. I never got a sense of what Peele wanted this film to be, outside of mildly shocking and thrilling. The worst thing a film critic can leave a theater with is confusion over what the package delivered was supposed to mean or infer.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: Nope’s staging is more naturalistic. Peele trusts his overwhelmed characters to forge a path through the story’s obstacles and frights without obvious metacommentary.
reviews.author: Stephen Kearse

reviews.text: It's really excellently put together at about every level, which is what I've come to expect from Jordan Peele at this point, and he didn't disappoint.
reviews.author: Vera Wylde

reviews.text: Despite some ingenious touches and a nod or two to the history of movie-making, Peele’s third movie is an incoherent, chaotic disappointment.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: A film that mixes elements of horror movies, with science fiction and even suspense, to develop an unpredictable story with touches of dark humor. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Peele's close encounter of the third kind at times lacks tension or something that hypnotize. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Nope is a movie about aliens in which fear comes too late, and collective survival is not a priority. That self-absorption is the allegory of the times. [Ful. review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fernanda Solórzano

reviews.text: A tense, gory and unsettling thrill-ride, it’s also wittily restrained, with something weirdly satisfying about the characters sparingly finally uttering the titular “Nope!” in moments of extreme peril.
reviews.author: Ben Turner

reviews.text: Peele’s terrific third feature, “Nope,” pairs old fashioned Hollywood showmanship with the director’s trademark blend of humor and dread, crafting a 1970s-style, thinking-viewer’s blockbuster with more spectacle than any contemporary Disney production.
reviews.author: Andrew Bundy

reviews.text: Despite the characters lacking a certain psychological depth, Nope has some interesting reflections about its production context and its dynamic pacing makes it entertaining. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Denise Pieniazek

reviews.text: Peele brings together ingredients of fantasy and terror that are pertinent to initiate reflection on more than one issue.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: A loaded thriller that doesn't reach, nor does it want to, the classic dramatic tension of a horror film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Bonfil

reviews.text: Yesterday's cinema allies with today's in order to help the hero capture the impossible. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Esquives

reviews.text: Like an amusement park—and of course, there is one in the story—the actors join Peele in putting on a bedazzling show.
reviews.author: Robin Holabird

reviews.text: Another Jordan Peele slow burn, and you sometimes wish it would hurry up a little.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: Nope plays with the human need for spectacle, not only the human need to witness a tragedy without feeling threatened, but also the need to be seen.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergio López Aguirre

reviews.text: Not only are the characters throughout the film guilty of the sin of gawking at and exploiting—rather than respecting—creatures and humans alike, but the film’s audience must consider their own posture. Do we find pleasure in the horrors we watch?
reviews.author: Brett McCracken

reviews.text: There are delicious popcorn-movie vibes and horrors galore, both funny-suspenseful and stone-cold bone-chilling. But most intriguing is the twistiness of how the movie grapples with its own existence.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: There’s obviously a lot of ideas going on, references, all that jazz, but it’s a frustrating experience, a film of diminishing interest as it plods along.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: Peele arbitrarily intermixes obsessions, questions, influences and his thesis, so much that we lose our compass and get lost in understanding the eye of the story. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Marcelo Stiletano

reviews.text: ... A story that runs out of steam. Oh, and also, long. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Writer-director Jordan Peele simultaneously heightens the audience’s anticipation to a feverish pitch while also mocking it. The addiction to spectacle will kill us all, we’ll just be too busy livestreaming it to care.
reviews.author: Gayle Sequeira

reviews.text: A fun experience that uses imagination to challenge and overcome its lack of narrative depth. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: Even Steven Spielberg would have to admit, “Nope” is one of the best close encounters we’ve had with aliens. Jordan Peele’s suggestions make sense. Best of all, they entertain thoroughly.
reviews.author: Bruce R. Miller

reviews.text: An immersive voyeuristic thriller that explores survival in the broader sense.
reviews.author: Renuka Vyavahare

reviews.text: Jordan Peele's sci-fi horror is mostly a "yup."
reviews.author: Nandini Ramnath

reviews.text: ... Peele -- aesthete, showman, and limitless auteur -- immerses us in a disquieting film that at times entertains us, at others, it terrifies us but always fascinates us. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: ... The most exciting piece of film-making you've seen all year: stealthy, ambiguous and constantly teetering on the edge of the iconic.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: There is a lot happening in this film, more than enough to warrant repeated viewings...
reviews.author: Dorothy Woodend

reviews.text: Perhaps as cryptic [as Us] but it concludes more convincingly, without having to be exaggeratedly explosive. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: Peele’s biggest spectacle yet, featuring stunning visuals around an incredibly talented cast...[h]owever, unlike Peele’s first two films, the social commentary and symbolism embedded in Nope sometimes overshadow the overall plot
reviews.author: Ron Seoul-Oh

reviews.text:
Nope absolutely brilliant. A subversive look at the horror genre, masterfully weaving in social commentary and packed with strong allegories among characters and themes. 

Jordan Peele continues to flex his filmmaking skills as one of the best directors.
reviews.author: Sheraz Farooqi

reviews.text: 'Nope' is an exhilarating experience that should not be missed by sci-fi or horror fans.
reviews.author: Kshitij Rawat

reviews.text: With its unique style, Nope may not end up being everybody's cup of tea, but it's an indicator of a filmmaker who is a master in storytelling.
reviews.author: Tatat Bunnag

reviews.text: Ever since cinema has existed, we've always been in pursuit of spectacle, [and I love] the way that manifests across all these different characters.
reviews.author: Leila Latif

reviews.text: An out-of-the-box scary movie that deconstructs the summer blockbuster with its daring cross-genre and referential cinema. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Elsa Fernández-Santos

reviews.text: It's extremely sophisticated, this film. And it's very mysterious in its structure.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: Peele expects us to react to disturbing energetic fields and intermittent power outages that never cause uneasiness. More audacity was expected from him. Do I recommend it? The answer is in the title.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Brimming with tension but laced with gaiety so as to never feel hostile, Nope is an operatic and sweeping thriller that celebrates cinema and simultaneously condemns it as an industry built on obscured violence.
reviews.author: Eric Francisco

reviews.text: Jordan Peele continues to astound, mixing his genres but continuing to amplify his own unique voice. This latest film is his most Hollywood while not being Hollywood at all.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: It is always exciting when Jordan Peele releases a new movie -- you never know which one of his anxieties he will put on the big screen or which classic movies the film buff will reference and remix.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: The result is overwhelming, electrifying and very refreshing, perfect for summer.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Andrea G. Bermejo

reviews.text: Nope plays with various elements and we have to connect them in order to have a truly fascinating experience. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: Peele's third outing is ambitious but unfocused. It's by far his best looking film and has a fun and suspenseful tone throughout. Unfortunately, his metaphors and symbolism seem, at time, to take priority over story and coherence.
reviews.author: Cody Leach

reviews.text: Jordan Peele is 3 for 3!
reviews.author: Kent Garrison

reviews.text: "[Jordan Peele] has to get back to being focused and letting us in on what he has to say."
reviews.author: Lonita Cook

reviews.text: Nope wears Peele’s typically theme-conscious writing lightly, sprinkling it here and there amid its creature-feature horror in a way that might only dawn on you in the aftermath.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: The result is disarming, terrifying and exhilarating, anchored in quirkily complex characters and, as the title suggests, a general sense of disbelief.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Meanings in Nope spring eternal, and they are surely too numerous to be absorbed in one go. A repeat viewing, then? I wouldn’t say nope.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: Nope may be one of the best acted horror films since, well, Get Out. A popcorn movie with a brain, Nope shows Peele has an ability to hold a mirror up to society while still being thoroughly entertaining.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: A gorgeously shot, if somewhat self-indulgent, saga of spectacle.
reviews.author: Trace Thurman

reviews.text: It's an exhilarating and fun ride as a result. Maybe more superficial than you'd expect from a Peele film, but no less complex in its characterizations.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Emerging into a culture that has always "had skin in the game", Jordan Peele's third movie Nope has plenty to say about Black creativity within Hollywood.
reviews.author: Kelechi Ehenulo

reviews.text: The social commentary is necessary and biting, addressing norms and ideas that have long been ignored by mainstream media and entertainment. Peele is a master in his storytelling and Nope is just one more example of his storytelling prowess.
reviews.author: Chris Joyce

reviews.text: Profoundly Herzogian in what it makes out of the film, the hallucinated odyssey, a unique quest... to capture in celluloid that strange unidentified flying object. Or identified: the white screen where dreams live called cinema. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fausto Fernandez

reviews.text: While you can’t help but recognize (and enjoy) the influences of Hitchcock, Carpenter, and Spielberg, Peele’s efforts to put his own stamp on the movie comes at the expense of character development, narrative cohesion, and story momentum.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Jordan Peele returns to form with his glorious, awe-inspiring third film
reviews.author: Hanna Flint

reviews.text: The sound design is inventive and slippery, always evocative, and Michael Abels’ score provides by turns, both bombast and insinuating grace.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: A better movie to argue about than to watch.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: It did not disappoint. The film mixes Sci-fi, Horror, and Western elements into one unique package. I loved it and have spent the days since I saw it going over it in my mind repeatedly.
reviews.author: Andrew Sanford

reviews.text: As far as film theory goes, it’s hardly revolutionary, but as science fiction, Nope is smart and entertaining as we’ve come to expect from an increasingly captivating filmmaker.
reviews.author: Christopher Machell

reviews.text: This is Peele’s most ambitious movie, and he completely nails it. It’s Jaws for the 21st Century. It’s a masterpiece of horror and science fiction, and it has one of the best third acts I've ever seen.
reviews.author: Mey Rude

reviews.text: ... Bites off more than it can chew, [Nope is] doubtlessly the lesser film in [Peele's] filmography though his creativity is always much needed in today's cinema landscape. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: There’s plenty to admire in Nope but the overall delivery felt convoluted and disjointed - it threatened to be great but never really got close.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: A reach-for-the-skies masterpiece that's ambitious and eerie, imaginative and expertly crafted, as savvy about cinema as it is about spectacle, and inspires the exact opposite term to its moniker.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: A solid, weird sci-fi thriller with horses and balloons.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: [Peele] may never again make a film so elegantly structured as Get Out (who has?), but the ferment of interlocking ideas here is so diverting it hardly matters that the film is more at home to a meander than steady ascent.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: It’s a riddle wrapped in a mystery inside an enigma, but it never quite unlocks its own internal logic. As summer blockbusters go, that’s more than enough.
reviews.author: Alan Corr

reviews.text: More a nope than a yep...
reviews.author: Demetrios Matheou

reviews.text: The script’s sharp humour, visual gags and expert line delivery provide hilarious moments of relief to the horrifying tension of this overarching predatory threat.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: Imagine a cocktail, so full of ingredients that you can't taste any of them properly. That sums up the muddled narrative of this film.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Peele is very good at building suspense and you are constantly wondering where the story is heading.
reviews.author: Allan Hunter

reviews.text: Everything about Nope is best when it sucks you in by surprise and swallows you whole.
reviews.author: Ella Kemp

reviews.text: Nope is nothing if not a spectacle. Peele wants you to look and he wants you to think about the exercise of looking and consuming – and he has all the tricks to hypnotise and bewitch his audiences so they never look away.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: The toy box is bigger but the cautionary themes run true to form in writer-director Jordan Peele’s alien misadventure.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: Nope is scary, funny, disturbing and sharp. But above all, it's expertly crafted spectacle.
reviews.author: Kip Mooney

reviews.text: Peele's layering of themes and ideas, which don't always cohere but form a multifaceted and thought-provoking critique, takes second place to a popcorn thrill ride of high stakes and bruising action.
reviews.author: Jason Di Rosso

reviews.text: Nope is an ambitious, vibrant, mix of genres and influences which, for the most part, is thrilling to experience even when it doesn't hit the mark.
reviews.author: Toby Woollaston

reviews.text: What follows isn’t some didactic message movie, though, but a sly revolt against the oppressiveness of that history.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: There’s nothing wrong with taking chances, but this effort plays as if [Jordan Peele] made a list of some of his favourite preoccupations and set about trying to paste them together with nothing stronger than unadulterated optimism.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: Flaws and all, the beauty of Nope is being two things at once. Art and cheap thrills, popcorn and provocation, blockbuster and brainfood: the old, mixed-up formula that is still cinema’s secret weapon.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: At times one feels as though Peele’s film is trying to do too many things all at once yet barely succeeding at making the points it seeks to make.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: Nope has a lot going on, but the magic comes from the way the elements work together. There are plenty of surprises here, but they’re not always the surprises you might expect.
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: OJ and Em find imaginative and practical ways to get themselves out of trouble. That’s why the audience goes along with them for the ride. They’re willing to let go of trauma the way children let go of helium-filled balloons.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Edalatpour

reviews.text: Nope is a film of many ideas, competing for primacy in a script that somehow dodges being muddled -- and instead hits the screen as a cohesive and engrossing mosaic.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: The more I thought about it, the less sense it made, but sometimes, in such wild and poetic endeavours as this, thought is the enemy.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Peele, really, is the magician disguised as a filmmaker. Nope is the sleight of hand so slick you’ll never question how the trick was pulled off.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: What’s a bad miracle, and how far will you go to ignore a potential backfire? Peele’s Nope stands more as a love letter to the cinema that raised us, scared us, and implored us to grasp impossibilities.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: What is plopped before us is a painfully slow, mind-numbingly dull film with so many story holes and lapses in logic one has to wonder whether any member of Peele's team had the stones to tell him when things in his turgid tale just weren't making sense.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: … a grand and fascinating spectacle for those who can attune to its wild and heady rhythms.
reviews.author: Anthony O'Connor

reviews.text: Its big reveal is the best kind: one that seems obvious in hindsight, but delivers a wonderful kind of cinematic pleasure, that of seeing a unique idea presented on screen for the very first time.
reviews.author: Tony Stamp

reviews.text: It’s a fascinating, unique and utterly original work, enlivened by some wonderful performances. ... The result is one of the great studio movies this year.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: This is big, compelling cinema that Peele expertly weaves blockbuster mentality and grounded terror together, refusing to sacrifice his unique vision in the process.  Cliché to say, but it’s a resounding ‘Yep’ here.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Similar to how the series Moon Haven and the film Lightyear give us a space that is inclusive and diverse, Nope reminds us that POC runs deep in every part of this country.
reviews.author: Jonita Davis

reviews.text: "While I do think Jordan Peele made a misstep by choosing message over narrative, after sitting with the film for awhile the message does make the movie a lot more interesting and entertaining." - Myke C. Town
reviews.author: Nick Wantsala

reviews.text: Brilliantly executed and entertaining...it's a hat-trick for Jordan Peele, the modern master of suspense.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: Nevertheless, Nope is an underwhelming film that’s still a fascinating addition to Peele’s filmography and proves him to be a versatile master of the cinematic arts.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: The violence of attention is a key concern here, likewise the idea that our biggest threats could be hiding in plain sight, but it’s worth noting that Nope also functions as a thrilling summer blockbuster in its own right too.
reviews.author: Joey Keogh

reviews.text: I enjoyed the dialogue, symbolism and themes of this film. I'm still a bit mixed on Keke Palmer but I did enjoy her in this role.
reviews.author: Justin Brown

reviews.text: I thought the two leads brought their A-game and Jordan Peele has cemented himself as one of the most interesting talents creating original stories.
reviews.author: Brandon Collins

reviews.text: It is a silly, nonsensical story filled with crazy characters, but it is fun, for the most part. The characters are worth watching and the story is compelling in its own way, the killer chimp subplot excepted.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: With the release of his third feature, Nope, Jordan Peele has solidified his reputation for making ambitious, interesting thrillers that mystify enormous audiences.
reviews.author: Soraya Nadia McDonald

reviews.text: It keeps you interested until it lets you down. Lots of potential but little pay off.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Whilst Nope nods to - and borrows from - other well-known ‘alien invasion’ films, as well as pop-culture horror, it also manages to be its own unique film, with genuinely impressive twists and well-timed comedy.
reviews.author: Jonathan Anderson

reviews.text: Jordan Peele effortlessly weaves a tapestry of horrific imagery and intense moments of threat, making Nope a very uncomfortable, but thoroughly enjoyable, roller-coaster ride.
reviews.author: Kat Hughes

reviews.text: Like all of Peele’s movies, you feel like you need to go back and rewatch it to catch everything and formulate your theories, a fun exercise that rekindles our joy for cinema -- the positive side of Hollywood spectacle.
reviews.author: Mark H. Harris

reviews.text: [C]reepy and charming, fearful and funny – a mélange of vibes that probably shouldn’t work as well as it does. Another excellent production from the mind of a generational talent. Say yes to “Nope.”
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: In the end, Peele doesn't illuminate those themes so much as he subsumes them in traditional Hollywood action beats... Still, a failure from him is more compelling than a success from most other filmmakers.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: More thriller than horror, with a twisted story that has deeper meaning if you look hard enough, but still a fun watch for those who don’t want to.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Peele wants to entertain as much as provoke, and he's not playing subtle. Nope is bold, in-your-face, and holds nothing back but most of all, is too much fun.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: Jordan Peele is no longer Raffi Benitez to me.  Now when I hear his name I think about the cinema’s new master of suspense.  If I met him, I’d shake his hand…and “Slap Ass!”
reviews.author: Michael A. Smith

reviews.text: Nope is still too fun and has too many effective sequences to be considered a disappointment. It's just not as resoundingly impressive as we've come to expect from Peele.
reviews.author: Gregory Wakeman

reviews.text: Writer-director Jordan Peele’s mysterious third film, Nope, draws on genre tropes from both alien invasion films and Westerns, but it ends up with something altogether original: a Hollywood spectacle about spectacle.
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: "Nope" is a funny, yet, terrifying sci-fi that will have you laughing while jumping out of your seat.
reviews.author: Susan Kamyab

reviews.text: Hunting for hidden meaning within the story and the pictures deepens the complexity of our relationship with the movie, but that's also a distraction from the simple enjoyment of its popcorn flick simplicity.
reviews.author: Melanie McFarland

reviews.text: Strong acting and immersive set pieces elevate its first half, but the weight of a disjointed script ends up sinking NOPE's gigantic potential.
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: Nope is fantastic! Includes great performances, immersive sound and amazing cinematography. A thought-provoking ride with shades of Spielberg, Hitchcock and Shyamalan. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: The cast is a blast and they carry the film– Kaluuya and Palmer in particular are a sparking set of contrasts, glowering toast-dry cool and pixie-ish chili-pepper hot.
reviews.author: Michael Atkinson

reviews.text: So many ideas crammed into one film and somehow it doesn't add up to a satisfying cohesive experience in the end. Incredible cinematography and a strong setup that doesn't seem to resonate as strongly as Peele's other work.
reviews.author: Jim Laczkowski

reviews.text: "Nope” is incoherently told. It’s a fascinating mess of a movie, almost never predictable in its messy nature, but devoid of the discipline needed to truly grab our attention.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: Jordan Peele’s ambitious project combines horror tropes with western vistas and wide-screen spectacle.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: Nope is a mirror that reflects back all the good, the bad, and the ugly of chasing after miracles right at us. No wonder all three of Peele's films so far have interchangeable titles.
reviews.author: Adonis Gonzalez

reviews.text: I kept wishing these actors were in a better movie, one that cared a bit more about crossing those t's and dotting those i's so you could spend more time enjoying their company and less time dwelling...
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: Whereas ‘Us’ had the feeling of a director straining to outdo his prior achievements, Jordan Peele’s third film strikes a perfect balance between inspiration and perspiration.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: What we've got here is nothing more or less than a director in full bloom, eyes wandering beyond the present toward both past and future.
reviews.author: Lex Pryor

reviews.text: This is not Peele’s best work, but it is well made and has much of his familiar inventiveness and novel approach to horror, making it a film well worth watching.
reviews.author: Monica Reid

reviews.text: Aiming for fireworks, he’s fired off a dud—though following two home runs, one foul is allowed.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: Peele rejects the premise that lies at the heart of the idea of the frontier: an unspoiled landscape that offers rugged and determined white men the opportunity to make their fortune.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Gray

reviews.text: “Nope” is an exuberant tribute to what would happen if all those “what ifs” about visitors from another planet actually happened right in the middle of the place where motion picture dreams are created.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: Does everything about Nope work? The answer is in the title but Peele's ambition, clear voice, and careful craftsmanship pay off in big movie-movie ways.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Rogers

reviews.text: Both his most impressive work from a technical standpoint and his least ambitious in terms of social commentary and thematic examination.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Peele’s exceptional script and direction, the story’s density, intelligence, and thrilling creativity are so strong the experience becomes visceral.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: Peele brings his comedic chops, palpable cinephilia, and an endlessly compatible cast together in a soft, often quiet tale that marks a clear development of his craft. Everyone will find something to appreciate about Nope.
reviews.author: Will DiGravio

reviews.text: I'm here to tell you Nope is interesting. Its combination of appealing ingredients fails to come together in a meaningful form, but it's a nice change from the usual big screen stuff.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: Nope is a well-made movie that will land differently with every viewer and have you looking at the skies a little differently.
reviews.author: Frantz Jerome

reviews.text: It may be over-stuffed with metaphors and symbolism, but it delivers it's central message with plenty of entertainment.
reviews.author: Sean Chandler

reviews.text: For all that’s here, so much in Nope feels lost or undermined in the stew of many things Peele as an artist seems hungry and eager to do. But we’re lucky to have him, even when the fact stands as a liability: Peele really wants to do it all.
reviews.author: George Elkind

reviews.text: For all its visually stunning and terrifying glory, Nope does have its flaws, coming off as overstuffed with ideas, yet ending as suddenly as it began. But Peele’s commitment to overstuffing, to truly going for it, should be commended whenever possible.
reviews.author: Owen Gabbey

reviews.text: "I don't think it's a horrible movie but I also don't think it's a great film. I think it's very interesting and whatever you take from it is what you take from it." - Nicki Dusse
reviews.author: Nicki Dusse

reviews.text: Between the watered-down storytelling, the hollow characters, and the frustrating lack of coherence between the interwoven stories, Nope is one summer blockbuster that can’t quite deliver.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: A new Jordan Peele film is always a reason to celebrate and while Nope will likely prove more polarizing than his previous efforts, the performances and spectacle alone are worth recommending the film.
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: NOPE is a valiant effort to be sure, with amazing sound design and the highly underrated Michael Wincott. Keke Palmer is dazzling. But interesting and quirky characters can't make up for the sludgy pacing, which is quite brutal to get through.
reviews.author: Lee McCoy

reviews.text: Peele is riffing in imaginative ways that kept me engaged and eager to see what all the fuss was about.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: It’s a one-hundred-and-thirty-minute litany of “nope, no, nuh uh, not me, not in there, forget it”, so Peele really knew what he was about, choosing that title.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Middling Peele may be light years beyond the usual summer-movie schlock, but even his most ardent admirers should be able to tell the difference between a film he has to make and a film he wants to make.
reviews.author: Bennett Campbell Ferguson

reviews.text: Jordan Peele's NOPE offers the writer-director's spectacular spin on crowd-pleasing entertainment, but the pace is marred by awkwardly embedded subtext.
reviews.author: Steve Biodrowski

reviews.text: Provocative themes are ample, offered up to viewers if they care to engage. That’s what makes this film one with great storytelling: it’s accessible in a way that entertains, while making weighty statements to prove a point.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Given the expectations for Nope, I’d call the movie a letdown. Nope made me long for the moment when the film would find itself, and I, in turn, would find it.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Jordan Peele's biggest film in scope and scale, but most constrained looking at the message underneath it.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: A rare misfire from Jordan Peele...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: There’s a better film hiding in this extravagant cowboy hor/mys/sci-fi. Peele’s followers and horror fans may ignore the lulls and remember the thrills. Others may feel frustrated waiting and waiting for something to happen.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: Peele’s latest winner adds a command of spectacle to his already impressive filmmaker toolbox.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: ...a chilling, chuckling science-fiction Western.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: A fun and suspenseful sci-fi western that puts a fresh spin on the summer blockbuster formula. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: Way too hung-up on theme and allegory at the expense of solid storytelling mechanics... the film improves immensely when it drops it in favor of just walloping us with immaculate suspense scenes.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Peele’s pacing is slow, the story dragging towards a conclusion that doesn’t seem worth the trouble it takes to sit through.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Peele is well on his way to being among those who have refocused the art form, and Nope will ensure that we keep watching.
reviews.author: John Wenzel

reviews.text: Nope is a stellar film that mixes comedy, horror, and science fiction into a beautiful cinematic experience to make one of the best films of 2022.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: Nope showcases a compelling spectacle crafted with remarkable craft and intelligence.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: Peele is paving his own way and creating his own style.  If anyone asks me if I’d ever pass on any of his future work, there’s only one correct answer… NOPE.
reviews.author: Michael Winkler

reviews.text: NOPE is familiar territory in the horror genre, possible aliens, falling objects, and animals acting weird as shit.
reviews.author: A. Tony Jerome

reviews.text:
This is about watching and waiting.  About what if that thing that you are chasing devours you? It's about spectacle - this awesome sight - but there’s another side to that. 
The dark daunting side.  Awe includes fear.
reviews.author: Eli Glasner

reviews.text: I greatly enjoyed the discovery of the plot’s daring and inventive twists and turns, along with the discerning and speculative ideas that they bring to light. By remarkable design, the movie is as full of action as it is light on character psychology.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: Made to be seen in a theater!
reviews.author: Derek Sante

reviews.text: Peele never achieves artistic unity... [He] wants to play both sides with a film that presents itself as a blockbuster, but it's burdened with all the worries of an art film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: The appeal of Peele’s ideas far outshine the limits of the execution here. But if this trend continues, it feels inevitable that balance will shift unfavorably --and sooner rather than later. Nope is good enough, for now.
reviews.author: Melanie Fischer

reviews.text: Peele’s third feature may feel like a departure from his grounded horror, but through his characters, he finds manna from heaven may not always be welcomed.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: Peele offers a science fiction movie that feels fresh even while he makes subtle nods to the sci-fi movies that came before it. Nope is a movie to which you have to say yes.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: This is a slow burn as Peele amps up this unnerving feeling of a close encounter with aliens. I could audibly hear people around me jumping and screaming as Peele pulls out a few jump scares.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: For all that it has on its mind, Nope doesn’t slack on being a suspenseful and genuinely scary movie. Jordan Peele is drawing on our cultural language for UFOs and then twists them in ways that are impossible to expect.
reviews.author: Ryan Silberstein

reviews.text: Peele is shooting for so much here at times that it is too easy for us to lose track of what we should be aiming at. Often it feels like a bunch of dissertations searching for a cohesive story that fails to satisfy intellectually or emotionally.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: Peele prefers to slow roast his audience by raising the heat under the pot gradually. We are cooked tender by the film's end.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: Nope is one of the most invigorating pieces of science fiction in recent years and sees a master of his craft delivering a spectacle where you can’t avert your gaze.
reviews.author: Christopher Cross

reviews.text: In this sci-fi Western, Jordan Peele provides some scary suspense - but because the characters are not fleshed out, the payoff is minimal.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Nope delivers a tale of extraterrestrial terror packed with powerful symbolism, potent scares, and tremendous performances from its cast.
reviews.author: Rick Marshall

reviews.text: The film is gorgeous, with stunning special effects and impeccable cinematography. The cast all perfectly play their roles, and the mix of humor, adventure, and drama works wonders.
reviews.author: Bobby LePire

reviews.text: Jordan Peele mixes and matches elements taken from big blockbusters and obscure subgenres alike to create a heart-racing nightmare that rains abominable filth down on its audience.
reviews.author: Alejandra Martinez

reviews.text: Si bien NOPE tiene sus fallas, sigue siendo una película bien ejecutada que cumple su propósito. Es un thriller de ciencia ficción lleno de suspenso que encaja en el molde de los blockbusters.
reviews.author: Josie Meléndez

reviews.text: His third film is the most mainstream, big-budget, and studio film he has made so far, even if some of the plot points don’t quite connect.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: In a world of regurgitated franchise reboots Nope certainly stands above the status quo, but when you’re this heavily invested in retooling and commentating on what came before it’s hard to see Nope as anything more than an echo.
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: Peele has made an intriguing puzzle with Nope. It’s gratifying when the pieces are put together, but the satisfaction is more intellectual than visceral.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: Peele has not become completely shallow. In a form more muddled than his best films but still effective, “Nope” is about our drive towards the spectacular.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: Those who see Nope might not get exactly what they’re expecting but they may enjoy it anyway.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: While less engaging on a purely visceral level then his pervious works, Nope remains true to Jordan Peele's reputation as a filmmaker who can pack dense themes and ideas into his work; this time setting his sites on Hollywood's explotative history.
reviews.author: Jessie Gender

reviews.text: Even a flawed Jordan Peele film still has a lot to offer and gives you a lot to think about.
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: Nope is Jordan Peele’s most giant and ferocious swing yet. With John Carpenter’s craftsmanship and a Hitchcockian mastery of building tension, Peele creates an otherworldly summer spectacle.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: Very few have delivered on such a viscerally entertaining, intelligent and profound level as Peele does here.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: While we still keep waiting for Peele to replicate the searing social commentary of “Get Out,” he instead produces a triumph of cinematic atmospherics.
reviews.author: Neil Morris

reviews.text: The film’s secret may take a few minutes to digest, and the final act feels slightly rushed, but Peele knows how to keep you on the edge of your seat and that he does. Like an amusement park ride, his third feature is tense, scary, and above all, fun!
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: . . . an oddball assortment of images, scenes and, just maybe, messages in another creative Peele effort that will make you both laugh out loud and squirm in your seats.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: ‘Nope’ is a spectacular Maybe.  Peele serves up out-of-this-world ideas, but we have to muddle through odd detours to get there.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: While certain sequences and elements feel more impactful than the film as a whole, it's an undeniably impressive achievement on nearly every level, cementing Peele's status as one of the most interesting mainstream American filmmakers working today.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: ‘Nope’ is an entertaining, thrilling, and just plain fun Western alien that further solidifies Jordan Peele as a modern master of the genre and its many forms.
reviews.author: Mary Beth McAndrews

reviews.text: It may not send shivers up anyone’s spine, but it will beguile, amuse, and occasionally offer a genuine jump-and-scare moment.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: The movie can be seen as a restaging of Peele’s own first film. Or it can be seen as a call to peers to find new spectacles, bigger, better and less racist than Kong.
reviews.author: Noah Berlatsky

reviews.text: When this film works, it is absolutely thrilling... [But] it feels like the script should have been tightened.
reviews.author: Lael Loewenstein

reviews.text: It's a scary phenomenon, and it's one that [Jordan Peele] milks very well.
reviews.author: Andy Klein

reviews.text: While Jordan Peele shows he can handle spectacle, the murkiness of the storyline, unlikeable characters, and lack of focus in the plot makes this a miss.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Jordan Peele maintains his track record as a master of suspense with the eerie to the extreme 'Nope.'
reviews.author: André Hereford

reviews.text: Well-shot and initially intriguing, but ultimately undercooked, uneven and underwhelming without taking enough risks. Jordan Peele knows where to take his many ideas in Nope from, but not where to take his ideas to.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: Born from the Covid lockdown of 2020 and one of the few positives to come from that debacle, Nope is what happens when immensely creative minds have plenty of idle time to do what they do.
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: One may not be able to tame a predator, but we can embrace cinema that makes us have provocative, awe-inspiring conversations.  In my opinion, Nope accomplishes all of that.
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: Nope is a spectacle in the least derogatory sense; a palimpsest of nostalgic blockbusters and Jordan Peele’s deservedly self-assured vision of Hollywood’s future.
reviews.author: Saffron Maeve

reviews.text: As expected, it is quite a spectacle and is sure to thrill and chill. While more sci-fi than horror, there are still some scary moments. Not much else should be said, but instead discovered on the big screen.
reviews.author: Paul Salfen

reviews.text: As far as Jordan Peele movies go, Nope is his weakest of the bunch. However, it still might be one of the best genre films of the year.
reviews.author: Deirdre Crimmins

reviews.text: If Get Out signaled the writer/director’s arrival and Us proved his first film was no fluke, his latest, Nope, cements Peele’s status as an elite filmmaker.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Nope’s junk pile of references combines movie and TV lore to no particular effect.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: Nope is a good example of how a film turns out when a lauded director... proves too fond of his own flourishes to trim the fat, to worry about whether his ideas cohere, or to respect the dramatic imperatives of the form in which he is working.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: As he pulled the rug out from under me for the umpteenth time, I sat in the theater muttering “Jordan Peele, you magnificent bastard.”
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: You’ll see a lot of stuff you’ve never seen before in “Nope,” and on top of that it is an impeccably well-made movie – so those two things alone make it worth your attention.
reviews.author: Mathew DeKinder

reviews.text: Peele explores another genre while still keeping a few of his signature elements to capture his audience. In the end, Nope will leave you confused and wanting more answers.
reviews.author: Alecia Taylor

reviews.text: Nope is impeccably acted, meticulously paced, and resplendent with bold visual nonsense. Peele’s “Twilight Zone” may be dead, but his leveraging of Serling's sensibilities into mainstream fiction continues that franchise’s legacy better than any reboot.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: Nope is probably the best UFO movie since Close Encounters, though the sense of wonder is here tinged with the sinister and unwholesome.
reviews.author: M.V. Moorhead

reviews.text: A little bit Close Encounters, a little North by Northwest, Nope is nonstop entertainment. Working with Oscar winner Daniel Kaluuya (his version of Cary Grant), Peele weaves a wild Western UFO tale.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: I never felt that engaged with the characters or, ultimately, the story despite some standout individual moments.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Peele’s most ambitious film yet, but also his most disjointed.
reviews.author: Michael Nordine

reviews.text: It's the kind of film where loose ends, and visible unsightlinesses are part of the process, allowing the writer/director the creative freedom to engage with his muse without having to get caught up in the preciousness of perfection.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: Nope grapples with enough issues of representation, voyeurism, exploitation, and spectacle to fill up 10 philosophy classes. Which is not to say it’s not just a straight-up thrilling and hilariously unhinged horror/sci-fi.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: ...a densely-layered analysis of where we stand as a culture, within a world where everything's made to feel big and consequential.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: Jordan Peele's 'Nope' is so cool it wears its sunglasses at night.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: Mostly it’s about Jordan Peele making an aliens-attack movie on a big scale but also on his own terms, with infectious filmmaking energy, and I’m here for it.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: As usual with Peele, there’s a lot unpack, what with the symbols and allegories that gesture toward the business of spectacle: wrangling the incredible and the tragic for our entertainment or curiosity.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: While there are a handful of scary and intense sequences, this is much more akin to a film like Jaws or Tremors than it is Fire in the Sky.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: If you're into strong performances and creepy images masterfully shot, this is your film. But if you're looking for suspense, jump scares, a coherent plot and motivation that involves more than an Oprah money shot, will you find it here? Nope.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: The movie mixes awe and wonder and loneliness and more than a little terror into a frightening brew.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: If 'Signs' was intentionally funny.
reviews.author: Doug Walker

reviews.text: NOPE proves that Peele is not afraid to take risks with originality while honoring the things that have molded him into the filmmaker he is today.
reviews.author: Jordy Sirkin

reviews.text: Nope is a twisted social commentary of the highest order.
reviews.author: Victor Stiff

reviews.text: Nope is a bloody, creepy UFO movie, unexpectedly gross in spots, with several different ideas knocking around in its head.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: Things begin to crumble when it comes to character development and the weirdly drawn-out final act, when all the film's loosely drawn threads are meant to come together and simply don't.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Peele remains a master of misdirection.
reviews.author: Odie Henderson

reviews.text: With Nope, Peele himself creates a spectacle, entertaining us with stunning imagery and bloody violence that's worth going to the theater for.
reviews.author: Brendan Morrow

reviews.text: Jordan Peele has again reinvigorated the horror genre with a concept that is equal parts unique and absurd, is stunningly shot, and imbued it with an ending that is tailor-made to be hotly debated and scrutinized.
reviews.author: Aaron Peterson

reviews.text: Peele has built a reputation that he almost bristles against in this movie.
reviews.author: Rachel Ho

reviews.text: Peele has always had an eye for bold, visual storytelling, but there’s a majesty to Nope’s sweeping shots of the California desert that feels reflective of his evolution as a filmmaker and of cinematographer Hoyte van Hoytema’s artistic sensibilities.
reviews.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore

reviews.text: Peele manages an agreeable mix of laughs and frights, even if you’re not sure what exactly he’s trying to say.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: A grounded, even earth-bound first act drama invisibly morphs into a spinning, scifi carnival ride of a climax, dropping some remarkably well-executed horror scenes along the way.
reviews.author: Johnny Gayzmonic

reviews.text: Some of it is fascinating and frightening, but too much of it is frustrating. And when a scary movie stops being so and drifts into incoherence and the nonsensical, it’s confounding.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: [B]y the end, it's little more than a monster movie that dismisses its best ideas and doesn't take the remaining ones seriously enough.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Nope is Peele’s most accessible, audience-friendly film to date, dealing less with heavy, social metaphors (aside from men exploiting animals for labor and entertainment) and going straight for the popcorn jugular.
reviews.author: Mark Johnson

reviews.text: Another game-changer from Jordan Peele, who pushes the limits of fun, fright and movie love to take horror to the next level. What do UFOs have to do with the violence eating at America? Say yes to Nope—it’ll mess with your head and pin you to your seat.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: This is the sort of film that encourages audiences to talk to the screen, to yell at the dumb characters. Peele shrewdly plays the audience, creating moments for them to cower, laugh and ultimately applaud.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: Never quite going where you might expect, Nope is a film you will be saying yes to.
reviews.author: Courtney Small

reviews.text: “Nope” sustains its momentum and cements a lovingly molded and gorgeous homage to the modern sci-fi B-movies of yesteryear.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Nope is a spectacular piece of genre cinema from one of American cinema’s most promising minds.
reviews.author: Maxance Vincent

reviews.text: Even in its jumble, [Nope] feels disconcertingly real in each of its precise moments.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: Peele finally cracks the creative code on the cowboys-and-aliens subgenre with wild cinematic flare.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: Like “Get Out” and “Us,” it is another resourceful meditation on fear and wonder—errant at times, yet strewn with frights and ever alert to the threat of racial hostility.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Jordan Peele takes us on a fun ride with Nope, but the final destination was a bit of a letdown. For some, it may even be a head-scratcher.
reviews.author: Emmanuel Noisette

reviews.text: Nope has only solidified my anticipation for anything and everything Peele does next.
reviews.author: Aisha Harris

reviews.text: At one point, OJ asks his sister Emerald what a “bad miracle” is; the answer is Nope
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Besides the story not connecting all the dots, there's still are a number of things to enjoy with Nope. However, I do wonder if director Jordan Peele's first outing with Get Up was a fluke.
reviews.author: Brandon Avery

reviews.text: "A movie that sneakily weaves captivating ideas about artistic anonymity within the pop culture fabric of iconic touchstones like “Jaws,” “Signs” and even “The Blair Witch Project.”"
reviews.author: David Lynch

reviews.text: “Nope” has moments of greatness, but the picture struggles to get past Peele's directorial fetishes, keeping the endeavor unsteady as it shares an interesting and unusual study of the traditional flying saucer feature.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: It is with a heavy heart that truth be told, NOPE just isn’t that terrifying --- or great.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: Incredible special effects, the most alarming music this side of PSYCHO and a concept from the depths of Peele’s brilliant imagination.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: Jordan Peele’s ambitious and inventive sci-fi horror entry “Nope” is one part brilliant and three parts frustrating.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: Nope is Close Encounters of the Third Kind for the 21st century.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: I felt like I was watching Jordan Peele's notes more than I was watching a fleshed out script.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: Because the story was so scattered and the action so random Nope did not work as a sci-fi film and it certainly didn't scare me like a horror movie should!
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: What fear and awe you still get from Nope.
reviews.author: Emily Wheeler

reviews.text: The writing, in a rather minimal slideshow way, lacks plot details that would help connect the dots and thread the needle, preferring to be stingy with any information that can illuminate or help explain the strange goings-on.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: Clever, but feels like every set is decorated with Chekhov’s gun.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: ...an overlong and uneven movie that definitely has its moments, but the whole is lesser than the sum of the parts.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: A skilled filmmaker took some great concepts and knew just how to throw them at a wall to ensure enduring fascination for us all.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: Peele delivers an enjoyable summer blockbuster taking a subtle bite at society’s thirst for exaggerated pageantry.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: While it is refreshing to see a filmmaker like Peele swing for the fences narrative-wise... some of it just doesn’t land.
reviews.author: Craig D. Lindsey

reviews.text: Peele is a student of how movies affect us, and "Nope" is filled with the kinds of things that make a movie lover's heart race...
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: [Peele] deeply unsettled me at various points in this film, which is about just about the highest compliment I can give to a director.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: He may not quite hit a home run, but Peele certainly swings for the fences, and a triple is still a respectable result.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: I speculate if the filmmaker is a one shot wonder. His latest is full of ideas but his exploration of those ideas needs to be more focused. I am disappointed.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Nope does indeed lack some connective tissue between its two biggest story threads that might help the movie be even stronger than it is. However, it’s so ambitious and interesting that it hardly matters.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: Peele is not just making an inventive sci-fi thriller. Nope is tinged with the acidic satire that suffused his last two movies, as Peele examines why the easiest way to process horror these days is to turn it into breathtaking entertainment.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: Disappointing. Tense moments but we kept waiting for Jordan Peele to deliver a mega watt jolt that never materialized. Expecting a clever horror film like Get Out and US, we grabbed the arms of our IMAX seats for Peele to shock us, but that didn’t happen.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: The film contains Peele's characteristic use of symbolism and Black American history to make his points, unfortunately these teasing little metaphors suck up the attempt to develop characters and tell a cohesive or satisfying story. Feels the same as US.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Some segments of the horror crowd responded with It’s not very scary. If so, then why does a bloody chimpanzee named Gordy still haunt my dreams?
reviews.author: Scott Phillips

reviews.text: Nope is as well-made technically as Peele’s first two films, but he seems to be regressing as a storyteller. You can appreciate his nods to the history of filmmaking, but the film is nowhere near as entertaining as people have come to expect from Peele.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: Nope is spectacular and intriguing, but also frustratingly incomplete.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: A sci-fi thriller shot through with elemental admonition, it celebrates the wonder of staring at spectacle while shuddering at the terror of what’s coming at us.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: If Get Out refreshed the genre in part by weaving in themes that invited a thoughtful conversation about race and racism, Nope is more modest in its intentions in a way that makes it more enjoyable the less you dwell on the details.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: A tasty creature feature and unsettling alien invasion thriller, Jordan Peele's "Nope" boasts visuals by Hoyte van Hoytema and the acting skills of Daniel Kaluuya and Keke Palmer.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Peele finds a stellar cast to carry his film’s vision. Daniel Kaluuya and Steven Yeun provide great emotional depth and sorrow, while Keke Palmer and Brandon Perea provide enough charisma to fill a room. But a special shoutout goes to Kaluuya and Palmer.
reviews.author: Joshua Mackey

reviews.text: [Nope] is, at times, comical, but ultimately a troubling anecdote about humankind, manipulation, and the tenuous, imaginary control we maintain over our lives and the environment.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: Perhaps it’s fated that a movie with ambitions [this] big would fall short of accomplishing all it sets out to do. But along the way Peele gives us one hell of a spectacle.
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: For all its fantastic showmanship and conceptual vision, Nope is also an accomplished third film that finds Peele’s ideas working in unison with his formal techniques to brilliant effect.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Nope is a fascinating film that is hilarious, terrifying and exhilarating in ways that haven’t been seen since [Jaws].
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: Though unexpected, Nope is Jordan Peele’s most ambitious and daring film yet. All the risks may not pan out, but Nope entertains and alarms with its awareness of where society stands.
reviews.author: DarkSkyLady

reviews.text: A bag as mixed as its combination of sci-fi, horror, domestic drama and downright farce, often mixed together in jarring, disjointed ways....Peele’s ambition and craft are obvious, but they’re not enough to make up for the jumbled plot.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: People keep comparing Peele to Spielberg or Carpenter, but all I want is more Jordan Peele. He’s forging his own path in cinema, and I am eager to follow him down to wherever that path takes him. Nope is original, unique, and wildly entertaining.
reviews.author: Alan Cerny

reviews.text: Nope joins a slate of films this year that make a case for the movies-as-a-thrill-ride argument, one that demands as big a screen as possible.
reviews.author: Hannah Lodge

reviews.text: Nope is that rarest of Hollywood beasts: a layered, piercingly smart original film which also functions perfectly well as a beat-the-heat summer thrill ride.
reviews.author: Oscar Goff

reviews.text: Nope is an ambitious movie that feels less focused than Jordan Peele’s other films, but nonetheless, Nope earns a Yup.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: In his previous films, Peele always seemed to be reaching for something. Here, he seems to be just groping.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: The best of its otherworldly images, sounds and shudders stick in the craw the morning after. I’ve already seen too many films this year that can’t make the same claim.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Nope contains all the chills, laughs, and lofty ideas that one would expect from the thriller auteur, but for all its ambition, it ends up feeling a bit scattered.
reviews.author: Dylan Roth

reviews.text: There are some fascinating internal tensions within the movie, along with impeccably managed suspense, sharp jokes and a beguiling, unnerving atmosphere of all-around weirdness.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: NOPE. Yep. My fave film my Peele so far, mixing ARRIVAL with HIGH NOON, a wonderful melange of tones and genre tropes. Whole cast is ace, but taciturn Kaluuya is just astonishing to watch.
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: Kaluuya is clinically depressed and his sister is annoying. Peele fails to bring to the UFO genre a satisfying story. A ridiculous ending.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: Jordan Peele’s newest is a movie that loves movies. I loved it for that, and a whole lot more.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: A sci-fi-horror-comedy that builds cinematic myths before casually knocking them over, Nope is one of the most effective and purely entertaining summer blockbusters in years, from a studio director at the peak of his craft.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: You give the first hour of this movie a pass because the second hour of the movie picks up and it's actually pretty cool.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: The sci-fi spectacular, starring Daniel Kaluuya and Keke Palmer as UFO-dodging siblings, sees the Oscar-winning filmmaker back in fine form.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: In an era of dumbed-down blockbusters that exist solely to placate their fanbases, the effort is admirable. The results? Sadly, nope.
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

reviews.text: It harkens back to the original summer blockbuster in the best way possible - with fresh faces and unknown threats that both scare and delight.
reviews.author: Kyle Wilson

reviews.text: A movie about making movies, the pieces of ourselves we feed into the Hollywood meat grinder, and our indomitable obsession with spectacle and its capture.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: Jordan Peele's sci-fi/horror/comedy doesn't quite have the cultural impact of his earlier movies, but it's an expertly constructed, hugely entertaining ride. Each intricate puzzle piece is perfectly fitted.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: A throwback to funny Friday night fright flicks like 'Tremors' or 'Signs', Peele's latest is an audience picture full of good, old-fashioned jump scares and blessed with an economy of scale.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: Did I like it? Yup.
reviews.author: David Poland

reviews.text: ... A big swing and a miss from Peele, even as he captures some haunting imagery and creates a tense, eerie mood on the ground and in the sky.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Peele’s highly anticipated third feature is, in part, a story about the irresistible compulsion to watch the world burn through the distancing porthole of the photographic frame.
reviews.author: Andrew Wyatt

reviews.text: If anything, Nope confirms that Peele is the modern-day equivalent to Alfred Hitchcock, a filmmaker capable of toying with audiences’ emotions with remarkable ease.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: Jordan Peele’s new film, “NOPE” does not have the depth of cultural commentary of his Oscar-winning script for “Get Out” or his follow-up, “Us,” but it is a smart, scary movie with a strong storyline, great performances, and clever details.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: ... A bracingly ambitious blend of UFO flick, horror, western and black comedy that’s full of marquee moments and bound together by a thrilling strangeness.
reviews.author: Ed Potton

reviews.text: Though philosophically unsatisfying in the sum of its parts, “Nope” remains thoroughly exhilarating as further proof of Joran Peele’s affinity for pushing the increasingly narrow limits of commercial cinema.
reviews.author: Carlos Aguilar

reviews.text: Jordan Peele leads audiences into utter bewilderment with the disjointed and nonsensical Nope.  Many of the disturbing details introduced have little to do with a somewhat obvious reveal.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: The entirety of "Nope" adds up to a sometimes wobbly balance of consequential and inconsequential outcomes because of the suspiciously selective and disproportionate points of focus.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: This is a movie with strange moments. Of the three horror films Peele has made, Nope is arguably the third best. But that isn’t a damning assessment. All three are worth the watch, and Peele has already effectively sold me a ticket to his next movie.
reviews.author: Jim Slotek

reviews.text: What Nope really is about are powerful entities that are hellbent on consumption, with little regard for the lives they are affecting, and we see that play out in both fantastical and realistic ways throughout Peele’s thought-provoking screenplay.
reviews.author: Heather Wixson

reviews.text: Every so often an obviously talented person makes a bad movie, and that’s what we have in “Nope.” The talent is there, the movie is dead on the screen.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: While it is possible one can have dumb fun with portions of Nope, the film clearly is a disappointment compared to what it is trying to build.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: It’s fun, but it’s not prime Peele by any means.
reviews.author: Soren Andersen

reviews.text: What could have been a witty, psychological exercise then jumps the shark, so to speak, and becomes a parody of 50s D movies.
reviews.author: Roger Friedman

reviews.text: “Nope” is another genre-disrupting masterpiece from Jordan Peele, whose intellectual, curious and playful perspective has become vital, and necessary, for the horror and sci-fi genre to evolve.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Some films preach societal morality packaged within stomach-expanding veneers of hollow goodness, and then there’s Nope. There’s Don’t Look Up and Jurassic World, and then there’s Nope.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: A fine Sci-fi thriller mystery that continues Peele’s streak as one of the best filmmakers working today.
reviews.author: Norman Gidney

reviews.text: Nope is Peele's most ambitious and weakest body of work yet. Nope starts as an intriguing and thrilling adventure but quickly becomes a narratively dense mess.
reviews.author: Sharronda Williams
