reviews.text: The film bedazzles with effects, loud sounds, and colorful graphics, but none of the myriad of motifs and themes it explores are fully realized or even coherent, and the plot ultimately betrays the film's title itself.
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: [Its] undoing is its insistence on remaining oblique. Not only is Nope a crushingly long 135 minutes, but those minutes lack even the pretense of narrative momentum...At this length and because Peele insists on holding back, the movie simply feels padded.
reviews.author: Matt Lynch

reviews.text: Nope is a fascinating, audacious genre experiment ... a cocktail made of equal parts science fiction and western, but with the spirit and verve of a summer blockbuster.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: While the lead up to the film was interesting, I do wonder if maybe it hurts the film a bit?
reviews.author: Stacey Yvonne

reviews.text: Though fewer and further between, it's a blessing that we still have filmmakers like Peele taking chances within the studio system. Nope delivers.
reviews.author: D. Patrick Rodgers

reviews.text: Spielberg's Duel masquerading as Close Encounters... doubling-down on metaphysical sci-fi, (this) creature feature suggests far more than it says in spite of everything shown... bringing the visceral bloodletting horror... Peele’s best offering to date.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: Excited to rewatch and shout about Nope from the rooftops.
reviews.author: Rogan Graham

reviews.text: The adrenaline rush of not knowing what’s coming next — rarely found in movie theaters anymore, unless it’s a dumb Marvel Cinematic Universe cameo — invades Jordan Peele’s “Nope” like a ruthless alien civilization.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: The confidence Jordan Peele displays is exceptional, and when his direction is concentrated, the full force of his artistry is unleashed with wild exuberance.
reviews.author: Josh Parham

reviews.text: “Get Out” writer/director Jordan Peele creates one masterfully shot and edited horror flashback in his latest, but overall the filmmaker’s ambition has exceeded his grasp here.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Jordan Peele's best film to date. Full of surprises & great cinematic storytelling, this is simply a must see - in IMAX. (Spoiler Free Review)
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: Hypnotically nightmarish, highly original (a difficult feat for this era of cinema), and thoroughly entertaining.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: The biggest surprise of the tight-lipped Nope is that it’s Jordan Peele’s weakest film.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: Is it all as effective as Get Out? Nope, but it is never boring and Peele keeps us engaged just wondering where the hell it is all going.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Jordan Peele strips back a lot of the seriousness of his work to make his more fun and adventurous film yet.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: Nope is an experience that's creepy, wriggling its way under your skin, raucous, and thoughtful in all the right ways. It's a spectacle about the human need for spectacle.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: Nope is Jordan Peele’s biggest outing yet. The third act is a massive SciFi spectacle that is undoubtedly built for the big screen. Hoytema’s cinematography is so unique, and certain visuals will shake you to your core.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: "'Nope' finds the Oscar-winning writer-director boldly expanding his canvas, aspiring to Spielberg-ian levels of popcorn spectacle without sacrificing the emotional and thematic heft of his previous work."
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: There was one horrible moment when I thought the film was going to reveal itself as a stealth Cloverfield installment. Thank heaven for small favors.
reviews.author: Keith Uhlich

reviews.text: Nope irrefutably advances the filmmaker to the ranks of his crowd-pleasing, superstar predecessors, despite the fact that his ambition and his discipline as a storyteller haven’t fully aligned.
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: Peele proved his horror instincts were first rate with “Get Out” and “Us,” so shifting to science fiction felt like a lateral move, talent wise. Something sizable got lost in the shift.
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: In 'Nope,' Peele wants the clouds to make you feel the same way the shark in 'Jaws' made you feel about the ocean and, darn it, he pulls it off.
reviews.author: Joey Morona

reviews.text: Spend two hours watching it and a couple more unpacking it.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: An ambitious, provocative swing, Nope feels like that increasingly rare beast: an original blockbuster.
reviews.author: Kambole Campbell

reviews.text: hen all is said and done and the credits roll, NOPE is what sci-fi should be. It’s imaginative, kinetic, smart, and one hell of a ride.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: Nope, Jordan Peele's movie about a bad miracle, offers a thrilling and humorous twist on Hollywood sci-fi - and serves as a love letter to filmmaking.
reviews.author: Ben Kendrick

reviews.text: Jordan Peele has created the unbelievable, an epic sci-fi film that will linger with each and every viewer for days and weeks to come.
reviews.author: Shannon McGrew

reviews.text: Peele’s made a thrilling, exciting blockbuster that also touches on the nature of spectacle.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: An artist at the height of his powers, Peele proves it's possible to rage against the machine and come out on top.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Jordan Peele’s masterfully audacious, wickedly funny and utterly outlandish sci-fi horror fable Nope is a classic example of a bold and original film that pays homage to a seemingly endless stream of great movies and yet is more than the sum of its parts.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Even a mediocre Jordan Peele film is better than the strongest film of an ordinary director. Nope is that mediocre film.
reviews.author: Caryn James

reviews.text: Jordan Peele does it again with Nope, a must-see horror/sci-fi film that delivers the original, thrilling movie viewers have been craving.
reviews.author: Caitlin Chappell

reviews.text: Nope, enjoyable as a spectacle but conceptually barely thought through, is all over the place. Peele can’t take just one or two interesting ideas and follow their trail of complexity.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: From start to finish, you don’t know what’s coming next in “Nope.” When was the last time you saw a movie where that was true?
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: Peele is three for three. You’ll spill out into the night jawing with your friends and gazing at the stars.
reviews.author: Jamie Graham

reviews.text: With Nope [Peele's] proven he knows how to make an unbelievably entertaining summer alien movie that can draw the masses … while at the same time warn people about the nature and danger of spectacle.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: Nope is a work of sly devastation from writer-director Jordan Peele that, like his previous films Get Out and Us, is a horror comedy with a speculative premise.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: Nope is a ride. And one again, it shows what a fascinating storyteller Jordan Peele is.
reviews.author: JimmyO

reviews.text: Nope has all the wonder one could want from a Spielbergian Summer blockbuster while still feeling utterly original.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Maybe someday Jordan Peele will make a film better than Get Out. But whether or not he ever does isn’t important when reviewing Nope. This film shows he’s still finding success when he steps to the plate.
reviews.author: Michael Walsh

reviews.text: For some, anything short of The Sunken Place will be a let down. Thankfully, though, Peele isn't afraid of the mess or the screams from the cloud above.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: A trippy, terrifying sci-fi Western that rocks a fascinating collision of big screen and real-world spectacle, and an electric performance from Keke Palmer.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: None of it would work without people. Palmer and Kaluuya could not be better.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: The result is a summer adventure blockbuster in the classic sense, a tremendous exercise in spectacle, and proof that Jordan Peele has only just begun to show us what he can do.
reviews.author: Matthew Jackson

reviews.text: Nope is good -- quite good in places. But it’s not great. In fact it’s not clear that Peele means for it to be, odd as that sounds. The story is bigger in scope but smaller in impact than his last films.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: Thanks to Jordan Peele, you're never going to look at the sky the same way again.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: There is something clotted and heavy about this film, with sadly not enough of the humour for which Peele justly became celebrated in his double-act days with Keegan-Michael Key.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: You might find yourself saying “nope,” too, once or twice, in a way that’s really tantamount to saying “yes” to Nope’s shivery pleasures, which feel both oldfangled and new.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: In “Nope,” Peele’s characters keep watching the skies even at their peril, unable to tear their eyes away. You’ll know the feeling.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Writer-director Jordan Peele’s third feature “Nope” is a big, bold affair, never lacking for ideas or set pieces. It just doesn’t work.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: It confirms the mojo of the Jordan Peele brand. But it also confirms that making movies with too much chaos and sprawl is threatening to become part of that brand.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: With some brilliant performances by Palmer, Kaluuya, Yeun, and Perea, Nope is the film of the summer. If you're looking for a film that will scare you as well as think about what's going on in the world, then this is the film. It is a sci-fi work of art.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Brail

reviews.text: Jordan Peele stages an absolute spectacle with this funny, scary sci-fi blockbuster.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: Jordan Peele's latest prioritizes iconography and subtext over in-the-moment narrative. It's still absolutely worth seeing on a huge screen.
reviews.author: Scott Mendelson

reviews.text: Nope’s disparate eccentricities are enough of a foundation, however stitched-together, for Peele to exercise the cosmic cinematic ambitions at which he clearly excels.
reviews.author: Conor O'Donnell

reviews.text: A film that does for open skies what Jaws did for the beach...
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: Nope is Jordan Peele’s Jaws. A chopped, screwed, and depraved loving hate letter to the summer blockbuster with stunning anxiety-inducing, white-knuckled suspense pieces that had my heart racing.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: Peele effectively captures the scope and spectacle of a summer blockbuster, packing it with chill-inducing moments, gasp-worthy thrills, and endless endearing characters, while continuing his streak of layering scathing critiques that keeps you guessing.
reviews.author: Meagan Navarro

reviews.text: With "Nope," Peele showcases a new sense of blockbuster flair while maintaining his signature gift for twisted modern relevance.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: Unfortunately, the writing does not come to par with a story lacking momentum and characters that would have benefitted from stronger development.
reviews.author: Jonathan Sim

reviews.text: Nope has an abundance of intriguing concepts, although their execution leaves something to be desired. It's Peele's weakest film to date.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: ..the spectacle works well as a magnifier for what is (as always) an intimate story told fantastically. I like the cut of Jordan Peele’s jib.
reviews.author: Sherin Nicole

reviews.text: As a sci-fi fable, Nope feels both more slippery and less viscerally satisfying than the more straightforward horror of Get Out or even 2019's Us, but it still sticks.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: The only sci-fi movie that might scare and delight Guy Debord and Ed Wood to the same degree...
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: [I]t’s a big screen experience that is as clever and fun as it is arrhythmia-inducing and stunning.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: A big, big 'Yep!' for 'Nope'!
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: Peele has crafted a beguiling world, one meant to reflect back our own in some refracted way. But he doesn’t turn his mirror at a sharp enough angle; we see too much of what we always do.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: Peele certainly has achieved something quite magnificent with this very different take on the alien invasion thriller.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Only someone with supreme confidence in his work would name his movie Nope.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: This is all well and good for a 90-minute parable, but Peele allowed Nope to bloat.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: Even when parts of it don’t gel, Nope is a rapturous watch.
reviews.author: Lovia Gyarkye

reviews.text: Does the sci-fi horror flick Nope live up to the hype? The title of this disappointing bore says it all. It's a rambling, disjointed, self-indulgent mess that does nothing innovative for movies about UFOs.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: With Nope, Peele once again proves that he’s not just one of the most interesting filmmakers working in horror today, he’s one of the most interesting filmmakers working, period.
reviews.author: Ross Bonaime

reviews.text: The film’s fantastical meta-commentaries don’t completely cohere but have a winning go-for-it audaciousness.
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: The Spielberg-inspired horror-tinged sci-fi features some outstanding individual elements – and Keke Palmer is a real scene-stealer – but they don’t add up to a convincing whole.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: Jordan Peele returns with his most visually ambitious film yet, a summer blockbuster that stands out from the rest of the pack with stirring cinematography and a real dedication to genuine, believable thrills.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: Nope feels like a major moment for studio blockbuster filmmaking.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: Nope has a lot of the hallmarks you expect from Jordan Peele, with added ambition and spectacle this time around. Not all of it works here, but when it does, it has moments that mesmerize.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: With stunning cinematic moments of pure dread, terror, and wonder, Peele has indeed delivered on his promise to bring audiences something unique, but at what cost?
reviews.author: Matt Neglia

reviews.text: Anchored by superb sound design and cinematography, 'Nope' delivers frightful awe with an intensity and terror that cannot be contained.
reviews.author: Matt Rodriguez

reviews.text: A thought provoking fun ride. Perfect for summer
reviews.author: Kathia Woods

synopsis: A man and his sister discover something sinister in the skies above their California horse ranch, while the owner of a nearby theme park tries to profit from the mysterious, otherworldly phenomenon.
